name: Luba and Lunda kingdoms
summary: Powerful kingdoms of the southern savanna of Central Africa, famous for sacred kingship and memory boards (lukasa) used to recall history.

knownFor.label: Lukasa memory board
knownFor.note: Beaded boards used to recall history.

location.value: South-eastern DR Congo, Angola and Zambia.
location.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

terrain.value: Open savanna and woodland, with the Upemba lakes and Lualaba River for the Luba and the upper Kasai for the Lunda.
terrain.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

climate.value: Tropical, with a long rainy season and a dry season in the middle of the year.
climate.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

resources.value: Copper from Katanga, salt, iron, ivory, fish from the Upemba lakes, and fertile river land.
resources.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

disasters.value: Not recorded in detail; droughts affected farming.
disasters.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

population.value: Unknown; the Lunda ruled a large area through tributary chiefs.
population.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

urbanisation.value: Mostly villages; royal capitals such as Musumba of the Lunda king and Luba royal towns that moved with each new king.
urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

disease.value: Not recorded in detail; malaria and sleeping sickness were present.
disease.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

migration.value: Lunda chiefs spread west toward the Kwango and east to the Luapula, where Kazembe’s kingdom formed in the 1700s.
migration.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

economicBase.value: Farming of millet, sorghum and later cassava and maize, with fishing, salt and copper working, and tribute.
economicBase.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

tradeRoutes.value: Trade in copper and ivory, later slaves.
tradeRoutes.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

wealth.value: Kings gathered wealth as tribute of food, salt, copper, ivory and later slaves.
wealth.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

moneyAndTax.value: Copper crosses from Katanga and salt bars served as money; chiefs sent tribute to the royal capitals.
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

inequality.value: Kings, royal families and titled chiefs above villagers; captives had the lowest status.
inequality.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

governmentType.value: Sacred kingship: the Luba king (mulopwe) held sacred royal power, and the Lunda king (Mwant Yav) ruled through tributary chiefs.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

succession.value: Kings came from royal lineages, but contests were common; the Lunda used positional succession, where an heir inherits a title’s ties.
succession.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

institutions.value: Lunda capital was Mwibele (Haut-Lomami), according to the infobox.

stability.value: Generally strong, but weakened by succession disputes among royal princes, especially in the 1800s.
stability.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

eliteConflict.value: Rival princes and chiefs fought over succession and tribute.
eliteConflict.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

armyAndTech.value: Spears, bows and shields; guns came through trade in the 1700s and 1800s.
armyAndTech.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

majorWars.value: Wars of expansion against neighbouring chiefdoms, and late 1800s wars with Chokwe and Yeke raiders.
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

territoryChange.value: Spread across the southern savanna from the Kwango to the Luapula, through conquest and tribute links.
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

alliancesRivals.value: Royal marriages and tribute bound chiefs together; Kazembe’s kingdom became a powerful offshoot.
alliancesRivals.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

inventions.value: Lukasa memory boards with beads and shells, used by Mbudye experts to recall history and royal lists.
inventions.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

scienceEducation.value: Mbudye society members kept and taught history, using lukasa boards and oral tradition.
scienceEducation.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

openness.value: Traded with the Atlantic and Indian Ocean coasts through middlemen.
openness.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

communicationTransport.value: Footpaths with porters carrying goods, and canoes on the Lualaba, Kasai and Upemba lakes.
communicationTransport.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

religion.value: Beliefs in ancestors and spirits; Luba kings were linked to spirits, and spirit mediums advised them.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

languageWriting.value: Bantu languages such as Kiluba (Luba) and Uruund (Lunda); no writing, so history was kept orally and on lukasa.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

artsArchitecture.value: Carved wooden stools held up by female figures, headrests, staffs and figures, especially among the Luba.
artsArchitecture.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

socialStructure.value: Royal families, titled chiefs, commoner villagers and captives.
socialStructure.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

sharedIdentity.value: Shared loyalty to sacred kingship and royal titles linked many peoples.
sharedIdentity.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

dailyLife.value: Village life in thatched houses; farming cassava, millet and sorghum, plus fishing and hunting.
dailyLife.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

neighbours.value: Kazembe, Chokwe, Songye, Kuba and Bemba peoples, and later Yeke and Swahili-Arab traders.
neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

ideasReligions.value: Spread the Luba model of sacred kingship to neighbouring peoples.
ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

colonisation.value: Divided between King Leopold’s Congo Free State and Portuguese Angola in the late 1880s and 1890s.
colonisation.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

riseSignals.value: Origins are dated before the 15th century by Western scholars; Congolese historians give the 8th, 12th, 14th or 15th centuries.

peakPeriod.value: The 1700s, when the Lunda king and Kazembe dominated large areas.
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

declineSignals.value: From the mid-1800s, slave and ivory raids, Chokwe invasions and Yeke conquests weakened them.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

outcome.value: Long-distance trade destroyed the Luba kingdom; in 1889 the Lunda empire was split by a succession dispute.

sources.value: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda.
sources.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda

overallCertainty.source: Wikipedia: Luba Empire; Wikipedia: Kingdom of Lunda
